outcome: Open a fixed-code garage door or gate from Home Assistant.

views.title: Room controls
views.condition: Tap the tablet, or approach it with Controls on approach switched on; lights, covers and timers appear when configured. With actions in Ramka 0.16.0 or later, one-tap shortcuts to a button, script or scene, such as a gate remote's, sit under the awnings, each behind Home Assistant's confirmation unless it sets confirm: false.
views.layout: Ramka landscape layout: 1024–1280 × 720–800 CSS px; phone/portrait dashboard not claimed.

setup: Use it only for a door or gate you may open with the handset you already have. A shared gate, such as a building’s garage, opens for everyone who can press the button in Home Assistant: decide that deliberately.

Wire an Atom Lite to a CC1101 module for the handset’s band (the M5Stack module for 868 MHz, tested; the E07-M1101D for 433 MHz, untested), set the DIP switches and screw the antenna on, following the wiring guide.

Flash the capture firmware over USB and press the handset twice. The same frame both times means a fixed code: paste one frame into the gate’s code file beside the device file and move it into the home’s private folder with domosenso private adopt. Different frames mean a rolling code: stop there.
Flash the device file domosenso add wrote, adopt the node in Home Assistant and press the gate’s button. Optionally list the button in the Ramka’s actions input.

states.label: Ready
states.headline: One button per gate
states.detail: The node waits. A press in Home Assistant, on the Ramka or a one-second hold of the board’s own button sends the code.

states.label: Send
states.headline: Send the handset’s own code
states.detail: One press sends the captured frame five times, about 9 ms apart, while the board’s LED shows blue. The gate’s state is not reported back.

states.label: Rolling code
states.headline: A rolling code stops at capture
states.detail: Two presses of a rolling-code handset give different frames. The node cannot send such a code, and the component ends there.
